Consider the following PR description:
AggregateError string formatting adds extra period in error messages

#### Description

When multiple errors occur during environment variable parsing, the `AggregateError.Error()` method incorrectly formats error messages by adding an extra period after each error, resulting in malformed error strings.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"github.com/caarlos0/env/v11"
)

type Config struct {
	Name   string `env:"NAME,required"`
	Number int    `env:"NUMBER"`
	Age    int    `env:"AGE,required"`
}

func main() {
	// Set an invalid number to trigger parsing error
	os.Setenv("NUMBER", "not-a-number")
	// Don't set NAME and AGE to trigger required field errors
	
	var cfg Config
	err := env.Parse(&cfg)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("Got: %q\n", err.Error())
		fmt.Printf("Expected: %q\n", "env: required environment variable \"NAME\" is not set; parse error on field \"Number\" of type \"int\": strconv.ParseInt: parsing \"not-a-number\": invalid syntax; required environment variable \"AGE\" is not set")
	}
}
```

The error message contains extra periods: `"env: required environment variable \"NAME\" is not set.; parse error on field \"Number\" of type \"int\": strconv.ParseInt: parsing \"not-a-number\": invalid syntax.; required environment variable \"AGE\" is not set."`

Instead of the expected: `"env: required environment variable \"NAME\" is not set; parse error on field \"Number\" of type \"int\": strconv.ParseInt: parsing \"not-a-number\": invalid syntax; required environment variable \"AGE\" is not set"`

This affects all error scenarios where multiple validation errors occur simultaneously, making error messages look unprofessional and inconsistent.
</pr_description>

package env

import (
	"fmt"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
)

// An aggregated error wrapper to combine gathered errors.
// This allows either to display all errors or convert them individually
// List of the available errors
// ParseError
// NotStructPtrError
// NoParserError
// NoSupportedTagOptionError
// VarIsNotSetError
// EmptyVarError
// LoadFileContentError
// ParseValueError
type AggregateError struct {
	Errors []error
}

func newAggregateError(initErr error) error {
	return AggregateError{
		[]error{
			initErr,
		},
	}
}

func (e AggregateError) Error() string {
	var sb strings.Builder

	sb.WriteString("env:")

	for _, err := range e.Errors {
		sb.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(" %v;", err.Error()))
	}

	return strings.TrimRight(sb.String(), ";")
}

// Unwrap implements std errors.Join go1.20 compatibility
func (e AggregateError) Unwrap() []error {
	return e.Errors
}

// Is conforms with errors.Is.
func (e AggregateError) Is(err error) bool {
	for _, ie := range e.Errors {
		if reflect.TypeOf(ie) == reflect.TypeOf(err) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// The error occurs when it's impossible to convert the value for given type.
type ParseError struct {
	Name string
	Type reflect.Type
	Err  error
}

func newParseError(sf reflect.StructField, err error) error {
	return ParseError{sf.Name, sf.Type, err}
}

func (e ParseError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("parse error on field %q of type %q: %v", e.Name, e.Type, e.Err)
}

// The error occurs when pass something that is not a pointer to a struct to Parse
type NotStructPtrError struct{}

func (e NotStructPtrError) Error() string {
	return "expected a pointer to a Struct"
}

// This error occurs when there is no parser provided for given type.
type NoParserError struct {
	Name string
	Type reflect.Type
}

func newNoParserError(sf reflect.StructField) error {
	return NoParserError{sf.Name, sf.Type}
}

func (e NoParserError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("no parser found for field %q of type %q", e.Name, e.Type)
}

// This error occurs when the given tag is not supported.

type NoSupportedTagOptionError struct {

}

	return NoSupportedTagOptionError{tag}
}

func (e NoSupportedTagOptionError) Error() string {

}

package env

import (
	"fmt"
	"reflect"
	"strings"

// An aggregated error wrapper to combine gathered errors.
// This allows either to display all errors or convert them individually
// List of the available errors
// ParseError
// NotStructPtrError
// NoParserError
// NoSupportedTagOptionError
// VarIsNotSetError
// EmptyVarError
// LoadFileContentError
// ParseValueError
type AggregateError struct {
	Errors []error
}

func newAggregateError(initErr error) error {
	return AggregateError{
		[]error{
			initErr,
		},
	}
}

func (e AggregateError) Error() string {
	var sb strings.Builder

	sb.WriteString("env:")

	for _, err := range e.Errors {
		errStr := err.Error()
		errStr = strings.TrimRight(errStr, ".")
		errStr = strings.TrimSpace(errStr)
		sb.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(" %s;", errStr))
	}

	return strings.TrimRight(sb.String(), ";")
}

// Unwrap implements std errors.Join go1.20 compatibility
func (e AggregateError) Unwrap() []error {
	return e.Errors
}

// Is conforms with errors.Is.
func (e AggregateError) Is(err error) bool {
	for _, ie := range e.Errors {
		if reflect.TypeOf(ie) == reflect.TypeOf(err) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// The error occurs when it's impossible to convert the value for given type.
type ParseError struct {
	Name string
	Type reflect.Type
	Err  error
}

func newParseError(sf reflect.StructField, err error) error {
	return ParseError{sf.Name, sf.Type, err}
}

func (e ParseError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("parse error on field %q of type %q: %v", e.Name, e.Type, e.Err)
}

// The error occurs when pass something that is not a pointer to a struct to Parse
type NotStructPtrError struct{}

func (e NotStructPtrError) Error() string {
	return "expected a pointer to a Struct"
}

type NoParserError struct {
	Name string
	Type reflect.Type
}

func newNoParserError(sf reflect.StructField) error {
	return NoParserError{sf.Name, sf.Type}
}

func (e NoParserError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("no parser found for field %q of type %q", e.Name, e.Type)
}

}

	return NoSupportedTagOptionError{tag}
}

func (e NoSupportedTagOptionError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("tag option %q not supported", e.Tag)
}

	return VarIsNotSetError{key}
}

func (e VarIsNotSetError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf(`required environment variable %q is not set`, e.Key)
}

}

	return EmptyVarError{key}
}

	return fmt.Sprintf("environment variable %q should not be empty", e.Key)
}
